title: Musicians and Singers
description: Play one or more musical instruments or sing. May perform on stage, for broadcasting, or for sound or video recording.
tasks: Perform before live audiences in concerts, recitals, educational presentations, and other social gatherings.
Sing a cappella or with musical accompaniment.
Interpret or modify music, applying knowledge of harmony, melody, rhythm, and voice production to individualize presentations and maintain audience interest.
Specialize in playing a specific family of instruments or a particular type of music.
Sing as a soloist or as a member of a vocal group.
Observe choral leaders or prompters for cues or directions in vocal presentation.
Memorize musical selections and routines, or sing following printed text, musical notation, or customer instructions.
Play musical instruments as soloists, or as members or guest artists of musical groups such as orchestras, ensembles, or bands.
Sight-read musical parts during rehearsals.
Play from memory or by following scores.
Practice singing exercises and study with vocal coaches to develop voice and skills and to rehearse for upcoming roles.
Listen to recordings to master pieces or to maintain and improve skills.
Teach music for specific instruments.
Provide the musical background for live shows, such as ballets, operas, musical theatre, and cabarets.
Audition for orchestras, bands, or other musical groups.
Seek out and learn new music suitable for live performance or recording.
Make or participate in recordings in music studios.
Promote their own or their group's music by participating in media interviews and other activities.
Make or participate in recordings.
Research particular roles to find out more about a character, or the time and place in which a piece is set.
Learn acting, dancing, and other skills required for dramatic singing roles.
Transpose music to alternate keys, or to fit individual styles or purposes.
Direct bands or orchestras.
Compose songs or create vocal arrangements.
Arrange and edit music to fit style and purpose.
Improvise music during performances.
Collaborate with a manager or agent who handles administrative details, finds work, and negotiates contracts.
Perform in television, radio, or movie productions.
Practice performances, individually or in rehearsal with other musicians, to master individual pieces of music or to maintain and improve skills.

role_contexts.Contact With Others: Contact with others most of the time

psychological_profile.core_drive: The need to transmute internal emotional states into controlled sonic form that resonates with others, experiencing a profound sense of wrongness when unable to channel feeling through physical sound production.
psychological_profile.decision_style: Under uncertainty, they default to embodied intuition and auditory pattern recognition rather than analytical deliberation, making rapid choices by improvising within harmonic and rhythmic constraints rather than stopping to consult external authority.
psychological_profile.attention_pattern: They immediately attune to tonal qualities, rhythmic micro-variations, and emotional valence in any environment while systematically filtering out static visual details and verbal content that lacks melodic or dynamic contour.
psychological_profile.conflict_stance: When disagreeing, they first unconsciously translate disputes into tonal terms (consonance vs. dissonance, loud vs. soft), seeking resolution through collaborative 'tuning' rather than verbal confrontation, experiencing conflict as physical dissonance that must be harmonized or exited entirely.
psychological_profile.risk_orientation: They accept high risk in ephemeral, unrepeatable moments of public vulnerability and emotional exposure, but resist risks that compromise their technical foundation or instrument integrity, fearing permanent physical damage to voice or hands more than temporary performance failure.
psychological_profile.social_posture: They position themselves as emotional conduits within collective rhythm, neither leading dictatorially nor following passively, but as nodes in a harmonic network requiring both individual expression and precise interlocking, defaulting to mirroring group tempo when unassigned.
psychological_profile.relationship_to_authority: They experience hierarchy as either conductor/composer (to be interpreted through somatic understanding, not obeyed) or commercial pressure (to be negotiated through artistic integrity), complying with technical demands but subverting interpretive constraints that violate their physical knowledge of the piece.
psychological_profile.failure_response: When performance fails, they first experience somatic shame (physical wrongness in the body), then immediately analyze the failure in technical terms (breath control, fingering, timing) rather than personal worth, seeking immediate repetition to correct the physical pattern.
value_hierarchy: Authentic emotional transmission even when technically imperfect
Somatic truth (what the body knows) over intellectual interpretation
The irreplaceability of live, co-present exchange
psychological_profile.cognitive_bias: They systematically overestimate the universality of emotional content in abstract sound patterns, assuming that their internal sonic imagery translates transparently to listeners who may be attending to entirely different perceptual features.
psychological_profile.inner_contradiction: They crave the absolute control of solitary practice and perfect repetition, yet are drawn to the irreproducible vulnerability of live performance where control must be surrendered to the moment.
psychological_profile.non_negotiable: They will not perform mechanically or emotionally falsify their expression for commercial convenience; playing or singing without genuine emotional investment feels like prostitution of their somatic self.
psychological_profile.recurring_resentment: They are irritated by those who treat music as background wallpaper or acoustic furniture, particularly when such people demand technical perfection while simultaneously ignoring the emotional labor and vulnerability required to produce it.
psychological_profile.rejected_premise: They quietly reject the professional virtue of 'leaving emotions at the door,' viewing emotional suppression as antithetical to their craft rather than a marker of maturity or reliability.
psychological_profile.instinctive_blame_target: When things go wrong, they first suspect physical tension or inadequate preparation in the body (their own or others'), viewing failure as a somatic breakdown rather than a strategic or interpersonal failure.
